The Watchman's Hour
A play in two acts
by A. N. Other

Characters in the Play
======================
THE WATCHMAN, keeper of the north gate
ISOLDE, a traveller arriving after dark
THE MAGISTRATE, who has not slept in three days
A CHORUS OF TOWNSPEOPLE, who speak as one and are never named

Act 1
=====

Scene 1
-------

The north gate. Night. A lantern burns low. THE WATCHMAN sits with his back to
the wall, and does not look up when ISOLDE enters through the arch.

WATCHMAN
The hour is late, and later than you think.
The gate is shut. The magistrate is out.
Come back at dawn, or find another road,
Or sleep against the wall and dream of both.

ISOLDE
I have no dawn. I have a horse gone lame,
A letter that will not keep till the morning,
And feet that have forgotten what a floor is.

WATCHMAN
Then you have what every traveller has,
And nothing that will move a bolted gate.

She sits. The lantern gutters and steadies. Somewhere beyond the wall a dog
barks twice and stops. Neither of them speaks for a long while, and when the
WATCHMAN does speak it is not to her.

Scene 2
-------

The magistrate's room. Dawn. Papers everywhere. THE MAGISTRATE stands at the
window with his back to the door.

MAGISTRATE
Three nights. Three nights and nothing in the ledger
But names I wrote myself and cannot read.
A town is not a wall. A wall is not a town.
Whoever taught me otherwise was lying,
And I have built my life on the instruction.

CHORUS
We were not asked. We are never asked.
We hold the rope and someone else decides
Which way the bell will swing, and when, and why.

Act 2
=====

Scene 1
-------

The gate again, by daylight. It stands open. The lantern has gone out and no
one has troubled to relight it. ISOLDE is gone. The WATCHMAN is still sitting
exactly where he sat, and the letter lies unopened at his feet.

WATCHMAN
I did not read it. That is all I did.
A small thing, and the smallest thing I could do,
And it will follow me the rest of my life.
